digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest storage
propositions: Event accumulation for queue and digest types is small (median 2-3 files per ticket) and storage is not the bottleneck (~2% of working tree).

Read cost is asymmetric: latest_ticket_digest is O(1) file opens, but pending_enrichment calls _events_of three times per ticket, opening all matching files (~5k opens for 3.7k tickets), causing the 20ms drain gate check to take 404-544ms.
Physical deletion of committed events does not reclaim repository space (blobs persist in git history) and breaks cross-clone merge reconvergence via git rename detection conflicts.

A suffix-lazy reader that opens only the newest file per event type per ticket, plus newer CLAIM files after the latest ENQUEUE, bounds opens to O(1 + k + c) per ticket where k is corrupt-file fallback steps and c is concurrent claims.

Merge-safety is preserved by reading-only access that removes nothing and renames nothing, leaving invariant I1 (never modify or delete event files) intact and the two-clone regression test passing unchanged.
